agent_output.affected_group: Commercial, charter vessel/headboat, and private recreational participants in the Atlantic dolphin and wahoo fishery (Federal waters, Maine to the Florida Keys), including vessels fishing with trap, pot, or buoy gear (e.g., lobster fishers) and holders of dolphin/wahoo operator permits
agent_output.change_summary: NMFS final rule implementing Amendment 10 to the Dolphin and Wahoo FMP: raises total ACLs for dolphin (15,344,846 lb to 24,570,764 lb) and wahoo (1,794,960 lb to 2,885,303 lb) with revised sector allocations; replaces recreational post-season accountability measures with new triggers; adds an authorized-gear exemption allowing vessels with trap/pot/buoy gear to retain 500 lb of dolphin and 500 lb of wahoo caught by rod and reel; removes the operator permit (card) requirement; and reduces the recreational dolphin vessel limit from 60 to 54 fish for charter and private vessels (headboats excluded). Effective May 2, 2022.

evidence.quote: DATES: This final rule is effective May 2, 2022.

This final rule 
revises the annual catch limits (ACLs), accountability measures (AMs), 
and additional management measures for

dolphin and wahoo. The additional management measures address 
commercial trip limits, authorized fishing gear, the operator permit 
(card) requirement for dolphin and wahoo, and the recreational vessel 
limit for dolphin.

The current total ACL for dolphin is 15,344,846 lb (6,960,305 kg), 
round weight. This final rule revises the total ACL for dolphin to 
24,570,764 lb (11,145,111 kg), round weight

The current total ACL for wahoo is 1,794,960 lb (814,180 kg), round 
weight. This final rule revises the total ACL for wahoo to 2,885,303 lb 
(1,308,751 kg), round weight

This final rule removes the current requirements for operator 
permits and permitted operators for both the dolphin and wahoo 
commercial and charter vessel/headboat permitted vessels.

This final rule decreases the recreational dolphin vessel limit from 60 
fish per vessel to 54 fish for charter vessels and private recreational 
vessels, excluding headboats, in the Atlantic EEZ.

This final rule 
will allow for the harvest and retention of 500 lb (227 kg), gutted 
weight, of dolphin and 500 lb (227 kg) of wahoo, on board a vessel in 
the Atlantic EEZ that possesses both an Atlantic Dolphin/Wahoo 
commercial permit and any valid Federal commercial permit(s) required 
that allow a vessel to fish using trap, pot, or buoy gear

The dolphin and wahoo fishery in Federal 
waters from Maine south to the Florida Keys in the Atlantic is managed 
under the Dolphin and Wahoo FMP.

NMFS is removing the requirements for an 
operator permit in the commercial and for-hire portions of the Atlantic 
dolphin and wahoo fishery as specified by 50 CFR 622.270(c).
